title: Wakelet · Customer story · Central Square AI
description: How Wakelet used Ellie to see who was engaging in their educator community, including the quieter members, and saved at least half a day a week.

headings.text: Two people ran Wakelet’s community. Ellie found the members they couldn’t see.
Ellie checks every Monday, without anyone asking
One ambassador. Four records. One person.
What Ellie watches for Wakelet, every week.

blocks: After Wakelet changed its subscription model, James Davis and his team needed to know who was still engaged. The answer was spread across documents, spreadsheets, Wakelet’s own data and HubSpot, and putting it together by hand took hours every week. Now Ellie checks it every Monday on her own, remembers what she saw the week before, and tells the team what changed.
their ambassador programme, with tiers tied to different revenue goals
on Wakelet’s community team at the time
every week, at least. Over a year, that comes to more than 20 working days.
The NPS and CRM report was built by hand from four places: documents, spreadsheets, Wakelet’s own data and HubSpot. It took hours every time.

She reads the same four sources, joins each person up across them, and remembers last week, so the team sees what changed, including the members who engage quietly and rarely post. Working from that, the team rebuilt its ambassador programme into tiers, each tied to a different revenue goal.

The same person shows up in HubSpot, a feedback survey, Wakelet’s own usage data and a training spreadsheet, under slightly different names. Ellie works out it’s one person, keeps that picture up to date week after week, and notices when it changes.
Same person. Keen last term and offered to help, quiet since moving to the new tier. Worth a personal nudge. I’ve drafted one for you to look at.

The team told Ellie what they wanted to keep an eye on. She checks each one every Monday morning, joins every person up across HubSpot and Wakelet’s own data, and flags what changed since last week. The numbers and names below are examples. Wakelet’s real figures stay private.
Which of our paying customers have an ambassador, and which don't yet?
Which ambassadors are making an impact, and who hasn't got going yet?
Ellie can draft a personal nudge for each of the 118. Nothing goes out until the team approves it.
Who is in our community, and how far along is each person?
How is one market growing, month by month?
Everything Ellie learns about Wakelet’s community stays Wakelet’s. It’s never used to train AI models, and the team can export or delete it at any time.
We asked James three questions. These are his answers, word for word.
JAMES AT WAKELET

We wanted to understand who was actively engaging with our community, including those who were participating more quietly, rather than making assumptions based on the most visible voices. After changing our subscription model, we needed a clearer picture of usage patterns, sharing and collaboration so we could focus our time and resources on the people who were most engaged with Wakelet.

We had a wealth of information spread across documents, spreadsheets, our own data and HubSpot, making it difficult for the team to build a clear picture of what was happening. Pulling everything together manually, including NPS and CRM reports, could take hours. Ellie helped us automate this process, saving our team at least half a day each week and giving us faster, clearer insights into our community.
“It helps you identify underserved members who might not be the loudest voices in your community.”

If your focus is on community and building something that goes beyond one-to-one engagement, Ellie is invaluable. It helps you identify underserved members who might not be the loudest voices in your community, understand their engagement and focus your efforts on the right people. It allows you to move beyond guesswork and make more informed decisions about how to nurture and grow your community.
Some of the educators James and the Wakelet team worked with, in person.
